How do we differentiate the icon in the taskbar vs. the native app

I'm a big fan of this value proposition, i.e. quick access to favorite site.

In order to change it to a call to action, I would recommend something along these lines:

Title: Add this site [directly] to your taskbar
Body: Get back to this site in one click from your taskbar [and with less distractions].

Further to note above, curious if we are trying to pack too much in here - one click, no distractions, Fx protections. Let's try one or more with the value laser focused on this being easy access to my favorite sites (time, convenience etc)

@Venetia Tay @Jeff Pfaller I'd hypothesize that the main user benefit of taskbar tabs is quick access to my favorite sites. Yes, we are making the implementation more secure/private, and that's going to be a + for some, but the benefit to me is probably quick access. So I would be interested in seeing a few more variations of the copy that lean into this user value - Pin your favorite site, One-click/easy access to your most visited destinations etc.

We don't control this context menu (known as the "jumplist") in the same way as other context menus. It will by default show these options for all running windows:
I can't think of any other action for this button that "Remove ESPN from taskbar" so I'm not sure it needs a context menu. Just clicking the button does that.

Would like to understand whether this callout appears 1) automatically, 2) on hover of the pin icon, 3) on click of the pin icon. 

I think it would be automatically... but in that case, I would want to strategize about how often. First visit to any site with a PWA mainfest? First visit to every site with a PWA manifest? I think it's actually something more like... we use some data and intuition to build a set of sites that WE think are the best showcases of this feature. For example, we would not choose ESPN even though it's a popular site with a PWA manifest, because it's not very "app like". We would choose GMail and Facebook though. 

Until you run across such a site, perhaps you jump to the in-bar message on the next slide.

We should consider the word "move" or something similar. Doing this will move the tab to a new window and otherwise not be disruptive. Possibly we should underscore that.

"Open in existing separate window" is not exactly right. Since taskbar tab windows don't have tabs in the MEP, clicking this would always open the site in a new window. The only distinction about what is "existing" or not is whether the site is already installed.
